default.notes: A Schengen short-stay visa is required, applied for at the Swiss embassy or visa centre serving your place of residence.

groups.notes: EU citizens can enter with a passport or national ID card and stay without a visa under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement; register if staying over 3 months.
EFTA citizens enjoy free movement in Switzerland under the EFTA Convention; register if staying over 3 months.
90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen Area. ETIAS authorisation will be required once mandatory.
Visa-free with a biometric passport: 90 days in any 180-day period. ETIAS authorisation will be required once mandatory.

RU.notes: A Schengen short-stay visa is required. Switzerland, aligning with the EU, suspended visa facilitation for Russia; fees are higher and processing is slower.

VU.notes: The Schengen states ended Vanuatu's short-stay visa waiver over concerns with its investor-citizenship scheme — a Schengen short-stay visa is now required.
